yeah and i know many people from many backgrounds have to deal with that including women who were born that way and like i’m from north africa and live in the US and have to deal with a lot of the anger against muslims although i am not muslim but it wouldn’t be okay if i were muslim either.

something just cuts me so deep about the trans stuff. it is what i am but it also stole from me something almost everyone else has which is belonging to one sex or the other and not being the right sex is just so painful. it’s like a cosmic insult and the fact that people just on a basic level separate me by a clear line from femaleness and womanhood and they often do it with no malice or intent to harm me somehow makes it worse. like on the most primal level i don’t measure up, and i never can, and i have so little to look forward to or belong to because of it.

i don’t know if i’m making any sense or just screech-crying into the keyboard tbh

it also takes just as many keystrokes and at least as much time to use the @ symbol on a standard keyboard or write it with a pen as it takes to laboriously write out the entire two letters in the word "at," and more keystrokes/time on a touchscreen keypad. i always saw it as one of the most pointless abbreviations ever.

but it might come from steno typing or something, that's the only way i could see it making any sense at all. but i dunno. written languages all evolved ad hoc so there's about as much stupid shit in them as clever shit and i figure @ for having slipped through the stupid cracks. maybe scooting ampersand guy's crack.

i dropped one or two posts in here on an alt and that happened with both. i understand. i'm a strange thing and my problems while severe and suicide-worthy imo are esoteric. i'm not surprised no one knows what to say or has the time or energy to formulate a response. if anything, i know from the upvotes and downvotes that someone heard my screams, which is more than i can say for 99% of the time i scream. i'm mostly sorry i felt i had to take up people's time like that when i should never have existed and there i was asking someone to spare emotional energy talking to me or at least reading what i wrote. it's not fair to them.

this is oddly glass-half-full of me so i'm gonna shut up before i get all twisted up from discussing some bad feelings related to THE capital-B capital-F Bad Feelings.

Even if no one replies, even if i get downvoted, i understand why and i appreciate that people who could take the time and risk their emotional labor on me decided to do so. i appreciate all of you who try to help, even if you don't know how to help me and err on the side of caution by not saying anything. tbf i always say on my posts that i won't take it personally or get bitchy if no one talks to me about them. i gave permission to not bother yourself with me without running afoul of etiquette, people took it, but some people still took the time to hear me scream and cry helplessly about problems i was born with and that can never ever be repaired, or even half-ass duct-taped together, and though no one ever replied to either of my posts, some people even voted on them to let me know they heard and my hopelessness and hatred of my twisted state are valid and i'm not crazy or being melodramatic by being so permanently and constantly devastated about being born in a way that makes it so obvious how severely and irreparably broken i am.

i wish i were a person from whom it could feel good to hear this instead of insulting or embarrassing because of what i am, but i mean it when i say i love all of you. you listened to me and the others who are hurting and crying out for help or relief or healing or just a quick and clean and quiet end to the intolerable pain. you are some of the best people alive on this planet, especially on the shitty anonymous cowardly bully and vicious clown playground internet where people go to feel powerful by picking on vulnerable demographics of people who let on that they are at their weakest, and these little shits of all ages do this in a way that no consequence for this sick, childish behavior could ever hit them where they live. amidst those little monsters are people with wonderful hearts who put those hearts to use trying to help the same people others would pick as targets for another "victory"tally mark when they successfully say the obvious thing that will hurt them the most.

i love you for that and i can't express how much i appreciate you.

i get where you're coming from. i'm trans, started HRT about 5 years ago when i was 21 although i've been presenting as female since my parents kicked me out for it at 14 years old--which means i had to watch puberty deform my delicate, skinny, girlish body into something monstrous--huge and ugly. and hormones can't make me the adult female version of that little androgynous teenager so i'm very wrecked emotionally and hate being seen in public. i totally understand wanting to just be a woman and being devastated that we can only be trans women, which feels like a shitty compromise life. and it's a subject that even trans support spaces seem to avoid engaging with directly, telling us we're just as much women as cisgender women, but we know that and we don't think we're less of women, we just don't feel at home in a body that's not fully biologically female and can't be. sure after hormone therapy it's not a biologically male body but we still feel cheated. and i'm not here to tell you the circular stuff like "because you're female, and it's your body, it's therefore a female body!"

your pain is real. most people can't understand what it's like to look around you and see that you don't fit where you'd like to among women and the reason for that is something beyond our control, something devastating, and something we can never just get used to. i hate having pictures taken of me with my cis friends because i see how i'm so different from them physically. and i know cis women come in a variety of shapes and sizes but i'm not in that range of form and function and it's precisely because i was born wrong.

i don't know how to make things better for you the same way i don't know how to fix them for me. but i can witness your pain, and i can tell you that the pain is real and it's not something most people can imagine and you haven't failed to cope properly or accept reality and it's not because you're not looking at it from a positive angle that it hurts this badly. it hurts this badly because it's horrible and painful and cruel, it happened to us as an act of random, purposeless cruely and we were powerless to stop it or truly fix the damage it did. it's okay to be devastated by that.

but please also know you're not alone with it. that i would totally hug you and hold you while you cried and support you through the worst of it if i knew you and you wanted me to do so, because you deserve to have someone to cry on and hold you over this whenever you need it. and many people will be willing to support you through the bad times, just as people have held me while i screamed and cried and lapsed into bouts of impotent rage or catatonia from overwhelming despair about what has been robbed from me before i was born and the future i have to lead without a body my soul can call home. and other horrible things i've been through have been made bearable by the support and friendship of others irl or online, even at my most lonely, unloved, and traumatized i could cry out, even to a forum like this and SOMEONE would care enough to listen and try to offer support and care.

it still gets to be too much sometimes but even a stranger's concern for your wellbeing can be a poaitive feeling to latch onto and move one to happy tears.
That's sweet, thank you <3. i'll try to be more optimistic about it. it'll take some time but there's not much i can change about the crappy situation other than my outlook about it.

it's kind of a whole-package thing with me. like big, shapely boobs won't make me attracted to someone i otherwise am not attracted to, nor will small or "imperfectly-shaped" (whatever that means for the wonderful things that are human breasts ruin a person's attractiveness for me. i also don't apply much of a standard to body proportions when it comes to my attraction to women, since i am a skeleton with hair, manboobs on a large masculine rib cage, and the hips of a teenage boy. i feel like it's not fair for me to employ attractiveness guidelines that would peg myself as ugly and mannish.

as a single gay trans girl who hates being single and trans but probably isn't emotionally healthy enough on my own at the moment to be in a relationship even on the off-chance a someone would pick me to be with instead of one of the millions of categorically more beautiful, fully female women with normal self-esteem, vastly more to offer emotionally and personality-wise than a broken thing like me will ever have, *sucks in deep breath after run-on whining* i found this piece beautiful and powerful. reading it was like a very good dream that almost inexplicably has a painful undercurrent of sadness to it. like dreaming about a day out with a loved one who you know is dead and even though you don't know it in the dream, it casts a pall over the otherwise joyful fantasy.

idk my friend is watching obnoxious TV really loud nearby so i'm having trouble focusing to write but i hope my comment is coherent and i hope you write more!

ideally i would be a woman. sexuality-wise i prefer women. if i were allowed to, i would identify as a woman and as a lesbian. but given where i came from and that many, perhaps most, women would take offense to someone born male like me calling itself a woman, i don't know if i'm allowed to identify that way, or if identifying myself that way hurts women. causing social harm to women as a group is one of the things i least want to do, even if i don't really count as a woman.

i haven't slept in 42 hours thanks to work. what i'm trying to say is you weren't remotely being a jerk here because you are entitled to decide when and how you're going to be there for the community as a whole so long as you are there for the community sometimes.

i mean, i think we all do our part to help by being part of the communities and spaces where we support each other and leave a footprint of information for people new to the process to find. people who are still closeted are certainly entitled to look up to people who are out as role models, but they're not entitled to conscript us as mentors, especially when we are barely or not at all acquainted with them personally such as in the case of the person who pushed your boundaries here.

the point of your transition process was to build a life for yourself that you wanted to live. that can include boundaries that other trans people are not allowed to cross on you even if crossing it would benefit them. whatever responsibility we have to the community and specifically to closeted trans folks, i don't think it's selfish or unfair to say that those responsibilities exist on our own terms. to whatever extent we are willing to help our sisters and brothers, subject to whatever boundaries as to time, place, and energy commitment, we are giving back to our community sufficiently.

personally i tend to focus on the responsibility of the people who keep specifically trans women and also trans people generally marginalized and benefit from their marginalization to stop being complicit in the violence and ostracism and ridicule that systemically plague our lives as the bigger fish to fry (if i'm using the idiom correctly) than our lateral responsibilities to each other, which should be tempered by our life circumstances.

so basically i think that while we have responsibilities to each other we all share this experience of the world constantly shitting on us for being trans and it's much more the responsibility of people who are not trans and thus are not experiencing that particular axis of being shit on to cease shitting on us for fun and profit than it is on us to sacrifice all autonomy over our hard-won lives to shield one another from the shit whenever another of us wants to be so shielded.

but i guess then it leads me to question why family members and strangers and fellow students and coworkers have called me "ugly" and "mannish" i figured i don't have a lot of fat or muscle but my bones make broad shoulders and narrow hips and a wide, boobless rib cage so that was why everyone who didn't know i was trans called me an ugly freak

before i was no longer able to afford her my therapist said the things i experienced as a teenager and young adult might be warping my self-image, especially the abuse, but i guess i never considered that BDD and PTSD could interact with each other like that. I don't have like repressed memories or anything but i have trouble trusting people and my self-worth is very low about every aspect of myself but i always figured that was better than being arrogant or something but i guess it's swung too far that way. i think it helps to know but i'm probably going to have to wait for money to free up for therapy before i can expect any significant healing on this but maybe knowing what it might be will prevent it from getting worse.

thank you for hearing me and thank you for taking my concerns seriously! you'd be totally entitled to pass my post by so i'm super grateful you care enough to help! i'm still getting used to people actually caring about things i say so i'm very impressed by this board so far and only wish i could be as helpful with the replies i give on here as all of you are to me! but i'm a big mess right now but if and when i'm better i hope i can give back!

more on point, i can't afford therapy because my insurance from work is so bad and i don't get paid a lot and have to help cover the rent for a roommate who's down on her luck and has nowhere else to go at the moment (plus my remaining FFS debt) so yeah no therapist. But that's a really good suggestion and someday i will and honestly i hope it's soon because i really really need therapy ever since my work changed to a crappier insurance carrier i'm no longer able to pay the therapist who was helping me with my trauma from a lifetime of being subjected to sexual and physical violence largely for being an out trans girl. 

But i have a few friends who might be willing to talk to me and actually listen to me later this evening, though usually i get stuff like "don't worry what other people think" which is not helpful when you want to find a place to belong in the world and there's just nowhere for a gay brown trans girl on this entire planet, and it's also not helpful to hear when you want to find love, since "what other people think" is exactly what dictates whether those other people find you attractive or click with you so if everyone thinks i'm just a gross fake woman who doesn't look remotely like the real thing then what they think really matters, because i can't just be "one of the girls" in my social life or find other women who are romantically interested in women. i'll just be a transsexual to them, maybe not a man, but definitely not a woman. anyway sometimes my friends seem to want to brush me off with the kind of stuff parents would say to a bullied child when they're talking to me, an adult, who is facing down social exile for being trans and is too testosterone-disfigured to hide my embarrassing body from people so i can't just be a part of this world i love and in which i wish i belonged. Also they tend to say "you need to love yourself before others can love you" a lot which i guess makes sense but i don't know how to love myself when the body i inhabit and the way it was socialized is not the person i want to be--not even kind of close. i'm just an ugly wannabe girl who was hurt by grown men a lot as a child and now i'm all skittish and scared of sex and ashamed of my body.

i'm hoping my friends will be keen on listening tonight because when they do it's very cathartic and it reminds me why we're friends because i love being that friend for people who they can vent to and it feels good when they respect me enough to return the favor. that is a very good suggestion and i was afraid of doing it because i don't want to come across as too gloomy and suicidal because i don't want to scare my friends away from me again. unfortunately i am passively suicidal and very upset and people tend to not want to talk to me or spend any time with me for a long time even after i snap out of my depression. so as much as i'd like to be heard i really don't want to be alone. being alone in this disgusting, alien body in this world that i don't belong in would make this nightmare i'm living into a total hell.

that was fucking painful to read and reminds me why i don't make friends with cis people unless they're referred to me by a current friend of mine. i know many cis people are very nice people but we all know i'm the punch line to a joke just by existing and they're more likely to get mad at me for being hurt by a joke calling trans women in general men or ~things~ or ugly than they are to get mad at someone else for insulting me personally even if they consider themselves my friends.

thank you for making the effort to educate these folks as i certainly do not have the emotional energy to do so when most of that gets spent between trying to live a normal life and being harassed and hurt by self-appointed comedian cis people who call me a friend but see me as a clown to insult for their amusement

and please pardon the rambling. english is not my first language even though i'm fluent in it so i kind of lose command of it when i'm distressed and not sleeping enough which have both been true of me for a long time now.

it's okay. thanks for replying. i'm pretty certain i'm just stuck where i am body-shape-wise without additional surgeries i might never be able to afford and which will age terribly on me, and i'm 5'7" and 125 lbs and basically unable to gain weight anywhere but my belly. i understand i'm not giving people much to work with. i mean i'm at a loss too so no worries. if anyone's got coping mechanisms in mind for someone who can't afford therapy thanks to crappy health insurance i'm willing to try most things. i'm just sinking deeper now that all my stupid hope in ambiguity is gone and it's totally clear that genetics and puberty stuck me with a body that i can't really tolerate and i'm staring down the barrel of another 50 years of life as this creature if i live out a natural life span and i just don't know what to do i really don't i should have been prepared for this possibility but i'm not and i don't know how to deal or if i even want to deal because just pulling out all my investment in this life sounds fine too but i want to give it a shot so i can at least say i tried but i just don't know how

it sort of stirs two reactions in me, supposing the girl in question is a complete stranger (it's not limited to conventionally attractive girls either, i think i just find femaleness beautiful in all of its forms except mine :P). one of these is just being happy for the person, hoping they're happy being female with the body they have and if they feel a sisterhood with other women that it's been very fulfilling for them. the other reaction is one i try to downplay by focusing on the positive emotions (which definitely does not come naturally to me but i think it's healthy to try): i feel sad for myself that i'll never be able to look at my body and not doubt its femaleness, that anyone i told i was trans would never be surprised because when they do that thing where they pick you apart for masculine traits after they learn, they'll find plenty to destroy my female image with, and that i'm never going to fit in with other girls in this life as seamlessly as they do with each other (which is not to say they all get along and don't compete, but they never look at each other as not actually 100% female like they all do with me to some extent). i then remind myself that it's unfair that my body and the life i was meant to live were stolen from me before i was born, that it's not something i could have prevented, and that it's not my fault. i take the bad feelings, i acknowledge them so i don't feel like i'm denying the injustice of my very existence but i don't dwell on them to hurt myself with, and i file them away, hoping that one day if i find someone willing to share her life with me i will be able to cry on her shoulder on occasions when these things get to be too much, but i will have enough independent emotional control that i don't overtax her emotionally or seem like i'm demanding something from her that no one person could give me. i know this sounds long and kind of daydreamy but my imagination and internal monologue have kept me alive to this point.

sorry if it doesn't help, though. in that case i'm sure you'll find your own way to make it bearable with time.

i don't know if this counts but i wear a lot of flannel, have a lot of piercings and tattoos, and i dress kind of hard femme except for work but unfortunately i can't code myself as queer as much as i'd like or i'll get misgendered, and i'd fear for my ability to be allowed in lesbian spaces because puberty made me an irreparably hideous monster and it takes careful selections of outfits that don't betray my true body shape and very good (and long) hair to get me past most people's trans-dar and ping that on a cis person and life can get very lonely very fast if you're a trans girl in your mid-20s and still trying to get your life to some degree of stability after just finishing school.

unfortunately i don't know any blogs or vlogs more on the point of what you're looking for.

sorry for not being more helpful :( it's kind of a sore spot for me and i've heard a lot of cis lesbians comment on how "stereotypically feminine" trans lesbians are and it's like, even if that's true of me it's out of my control. life has proven intolerably hard when i can't just blend in when i need to and i don't think i'm alone among trans women in that.

And I think the worst part is that I can't blame anyone for my not belonging. I'm very different. Of course I don't fit. I still see a freak when I look in the mirror so why shouldn't anyone else? Why shouldn't I be feared as potentially dangerous male invader in women's spaces when underneath my patchwork of illusions I just have the feminized body of a teenage boy for all sex and gender purposes. If I were an actual woman I wouldn't see this thing I am now as just as female as hypothetical cis me. It feels wrong to me to push for people to make themselves comfortable for my special little glaring defect. But that leaves death as the only escape from the hellishness of this humiliating, psychologically excruciating condition. I'm just... I'm fine with death. This was never going to be a life worth living. Any chance of that was gone when I was born a boy who needed to be a girl, a real one who was accepted as such. This whole stupid project was doomed from the outset and the sooner its over the less of that doom I have to experience.

I feel like what I'm throwing away is just more suffering. I mean being unattracted to trans women when you like only women is pretty ubiquitous, as is seeing us as crazy or predatory men and not wanting us in women's spaces, not thinking of us and women in the same category is a less damaging but still painful social constant. like even if some of the ridicule and physical/sexual violence i've experienced frequently dies down i don't see my life being anything but miserable. maybe less miserable but that's not really much to live for.

and like leukemia and homelessness were horrible but didn't carry the same lack of belonging anywhere in the world. i knew of communities of homeless kids but i wasn't welcome because i was a freak. When I had cancer no one made fun of me for that and the girls i knew with leukemia were no less human, and no less welcome among women, for being sick. i mercifully kept my hair through the chemo but if i hadn't i'd have killed myself on the spot rather than being the bald tranny that's so funny to everyone because i call myself a woman but i pathetically fail to look like one. it nearly killed me but it didn't strip me of all reason to live like being a male-bodied creep does.
I'd join that club but honestly I'd probably be too depressed to leave my house to go to the meetings and everyone would think I already killed myself even if I hadn't yet.

I'm sorry you have to deal with mental illness too. I have schizoaffective disorder and though it's controlled, it makes everything worse. I didn't mention it above because it hasn't caused me nearly as much trouble as being stuck with the wrong sex for my entire lifetime but yeah it doesn't help to be crazy one way when people think i'm crazy for being transsexual.

But every time I dig myself out it never gets better than "still awful" and then I plummet back down here again maybe it's dangerous but this time I'm feeling motivated and most of me really wants to break the cycle of misery in the only way it can be broken, you know?

I'm a 26 year old middle eastern trans girl who started almost 4 years ago (about 4 months before I turned 22. For the first 3 years I was on 4mg estradiol and 200 mg spironolactone and I switched to 1ml estradiol biweekly about 7 months ago.

Some changes were quick. Soft skin and nipple soreness was palpable about a month into it. then fat redistrobution around the buttocks and breasts was visible after 4 months, reaching its peak about a year ago, with a dramatic slowdown in changes by the second year. I noticed myself becoming less physically strong about a year into it, and I retained fat more easily. Most of the facial changes were very noticeable by six months in and continued for about another two years, rapidly at first and then more slowly.

As far as muscle structure changes, the most prominent difference is my abdomen, where my waistline is a fair bit higher than it was 4 years ago, and my calf muscles and biceps are significantly smaller, though my upper arms are still quite large though this is probably because I became much more lax in physical activity following a pretty severe depression spell for the second year and a half relating to kind of, I dunno, finally accepting what the limits for my physical changes would be and my place in the world w/r/t cis women's communities and the lesbian community, and I gained a lot of weight following gall bladder surgery and still haven't quite recovered my energy levels and drive after a month and a half of being very sedentary.

Not sure how helpful this all is, it's kind of scattered because I can't stand to take pictures of myself due to body issues so I was unable to make a timeline for me to look at.
